name: The flat's corridor between the bedrooms (Singapore): test level eval2, Packing Day from scratch; from the owner's photograph of 24 Oct 2026, not kept
setting: Cosy and plain: a short narrow corridor in a Singapore flat on a rainy December afternoon, empty of people.
palette: the walls are plain white, with no painted band; the band line is only the height of a door handle, 36% of the way up the back wall from the floor; the floor is pale stone tiles with a faint sheen; dark honey-coloured wooden doors, frames and skirting boards along every wall
box: a narrow deep box in one-point perspective: a back wall only as wide as a corridor, long side walls, a thin strip of ceiling with one small round light, a floor band; flat plain walls meeting at plain corners, with no piers, columns, recesses, steps or returns anywhere
light: no window of its own: a small round ceiling light, and grey daylight reaching in from the dining end at the far end of the corridor and through the two open bedroom doors

c1.name: the children's door (north), the end of the corridor
c1.light: grey daylight comes out of the open doorway itself, from the children's window beyond; the corridor walls either side are lit by the ceiling light

objects.label: the children's open dark wooden door
objects.text: at the end of the corridor, the children's doorway with a dark honey wood frame; the dark honey wooden door is hinged on the right-hand jamb and stands fully open, swung away into the room toward the right, and through the doorway a glimpse of the children's room as its own walls show it: white walls with low white skirting boards, a pale honey wood floor and a grey rug, the glass wall with rain and a white bunk bed's end covered in tiny stickers at the right, grey daylight
objects.size: the door reaches almost to the ceiling strip

c2.name: Mary's door (east), the first on the left walking in
c2.light: grey daylight comes out of Mary's open doorway at the left, from her window beyond; the rest of the wall is lit by the ceiling light

objects.label: Mary's open dark wooden door
objects.text: Mary's doorway at the left: a dark honey wood frame, the dark honey wooden door hinged on the left-hand jamb and standing fully open, swung away into her room toward the left, and through the doorway a glimpse of her room as its own walls show it: white walls with low honey wood skirting boards, a pale honey wood floor, the end of a grey sofa at the left, a striped rug, the window with rain ahead, grey daylight
objects.size: the door reaches almost to the ceiling strip

objects.label: framed picture
objects.text: a small framed picture with a dark frame on the white wall, between Mary's door and the second door, at a grown-up's eye height

objects.label: a second dark wooden door, closed
objects.text: further along at the right, a second dark wooden door, closed, with a brass handle
objects.size: the door reaches almost to the ceiling strip

c3.name: the double doors (south), the far end of the corridor and the turn to the dining end
c3.light: grey daylight comes round the corner from the dining end at the right, bright on the stone floor there; the double doors at the end are in softer ceiling light

objects.label: closed double doors
objects.text: at the end of the corridor, a pair of tall dark wooden double doors, closed, with two small brass handles meeting in the middle
objects.size: reaching almost to the ceiling strip

objects.label: the turn to the dining end
objects.text: at the right the corridor opens into the dining end: bright grey daylight, the same pale stone tiles and dark honey wood skirting boards continuing round the corner, the corner of a pine dining table and a wooden chair, a white wall beyond
objects.size: an opening the full height of the wall

c4.name: the wall opposite Mary's door (west)
c4.light: lit by the ceiling light, with grey daylight from Mary's doorway behind the viewer

objects.label: a light switch
objects.text: a single white light switch on the plain white wall at a grown-up's shoulder height

objects.label: plain wall and wood skirting
objects.text: a plain white wall with a low dark honey wood skirting board, nothing else on it

doors.hinge: on the right-hand jamb seen from the corridor (the children's room's east jamb)
doors.swing: away from the corridor, into the children's room, toward the right

doors.hinge: on the left-hand jamb seen from the corridor (Mary's room's north jamb)
doors.swing: away from the corridor, into Mary's room, toward the left

order.c2: left to right: Mary's door at the north end, then the framed picture, then the second closed door (the owner's photograph, from the children's doorway: Mary's door first on the left)
